title: Job Readiness Assessment
description: A full mixed assessment modelled on employer screening batteries: cognitive ability, software engineering, Python, AI, coding, workplace judgement and written communication.
instructions: This is a timed, mixed assessment like a real employer screening test.
Questions appear one at a time. Once you move on, you cannot go back.
The timer keeps running even if you close the tab. When it runs out, your answers are submitted automatically.
You can run your code against the example tests. Hidden tests are used for scoring.
Work alone without looking things up, as you would on the real test.

title: Numerical Reasoning
description: Percentages, ratios, rates and reading data from tables, under time pressure.
instructions: You may use a calculator and scratch paper.
Read every table carefully. Many wrong answers come from using the wrong base value.

title: Critical Thinking
description: Deductive logic, evaluating arguments, spotting assumptions, and ordering puzzles.
instructions: Use only the information given. Don't bring in outside assumptions.
Watch for 'must be true' versus 'could be true'.

title: Attention to Detail
description: Spot small differences in codes, records, configurations and calculations.
instructions: Accuracy matters more than speed, but the time is tight.

title: Software Engineering Fundamentals
description: Git, HTTP and APIs, SQL, data structures, complexity, testing, security and design principles.
instructions: Questions cover the breadth expected of a junior engineer.

title: Python Knowledge
description: Predict outputs and spot gotchas: references, mutability, closures, generators, exceptions.
instructions: Work out the code in your head. Don't run it.

title: AI & ML Fundamentals
description: LLM concepts, RAG, embeddings, evaluation metrics, overfitting and AI safety.
instructions: Covers the AI concepts an entry-level AI engineer is expected to know.

title: Python Coding Challenge
description: Two timed coding problems graded by hidden test cases, like a real coding screen.
instructions: Implement the function using the exact name from the starter code.
Use Run to check your code against the example tests. Your score comes from all tests, including hidden edge cases.
Think about edge cases (empty input, duplicates, ties) before you submit.
Partial credit is given per test case passed.

title: Workplace Situational Judgement
description: Realistic engineering workplace scenarios: teamwork, escalation, communication and professionalism.
instructions: Choose the MOST effective response. Several options may be reasonable.
Partial credit is given for acceptable but less effective responses.

title: Written Communication
description: Write workplace messages: explaining tech to non-technical people, incident updates, pushback and code reviews. Graded by AI against a rubric.
instructions: Stick to the word limits; going far over costs points, as it would with a real reader.
Write for the audience named in the question.
Answers are graded by AI against a hiring rubric after you submit.
